name: Beeler Park Flats
award: 2024 Federal 9% and state housing tax credits (Round One)
headline: Mile High Development is building Beeler Park Flats, a five-story, 64-unit family rental in the Beeler Park area of Denver's Central Park neighborhood for households at 30% to 60% AMI, financed with a 2024 Round One 9% and state credit award, a $2.1M City of Denver loan and KeyBank debt and equity.
why_it_matters: It is an example of affordable housing required by the Central Park master plan being carved out of a market-rate developer's parcel, with the city's linkage-fee fund and a 60-year covenant filling the gap.

status.label: Financing closed (August 2025, per KeyBank); 64-unit building permit issued 2025-09-04 (inferred to be this project); completion not confirmed
status.detail: KeyBank lists a construction loan, LIHTC equity and Freddie Mac forward commitment for Beeler Park Flats dated August 2025. Denver's permit data shows a new-building permit for 64 units at 5601 N Chester Way in Central Park issued 2025-09-04 (valuation $13.2M), with follow-on permits through 2026-10-08 and no certificate of occupancy; matching that permit to this project is inferred from the unit count, location and timing.

next_step: Watch Denver's permit data for a certificate of occupancy at 5601 N Chester Way, and for lease-up by the property manager.

key_numbers.meaning: Mostly family-sized: 51 two-bedroom and 8 three-bedroom units; 7 units at 30% AMI.

key_numbers.meaning: About $14.1M in federal credit over 10 years (inferred from the annual amount). The application had asked for $1,450,000 a year.

key_numbers.meaning: Non-recourse cash-flow loan from the Affordable Housing Linkage Fee Fund, approved by council 2025-08-11 (CR25-0809), with a 60-year affordability covenant.

background.text: Land deal: the applicant says a market-rate developer did due diligence for a multifamily project on the property and then agreed to sell part of it to Mile High Development to satisfy the Central Park master plan's affordable housing requirement.
The applicant says it could not use income averaging because the Central Park requirement caps these units at 60% AMI or below; the market study had recommended more 40% and 80% units.
This was a repeat attempt: Mile High Development had submitted an earlier LIHTC application for the site in 2020, and the 2024 version proposes more family units in a smaller project.

Front Porch reported in February 2025 that construction was expected to start that August and take 13 months, with ground-floor office space for the Foundation for Sustainable Urban Communities, and that a second building is planned but depends on more tax credits.
Denver's loan approval: the Safety, Housing, Education & Homelessness Committee approved filing by consent on 2025-06-04 and City Council adopted resolution CR25-0809 on 2025-08-11.

Denver's loan agreement fixes the bedroom-by-income split: 1BR 1/1/1/2, 2BR 5/5/17/24 and 3BR 1/1/3/3 at 30/40/50/60% AMI, and requires at least 5% mobility-accessible and 2% hearing/vision-accessible units, plus an affirmative marketing plan.
The applicant cites a 14.9% capture rate and a Phase I with no recognized environmental conditions; the nearest family LIHTC properties are Northfield Apartments and Pinecrest, about 1.5 miles away.

CHFA and the city loan request give the address as 5652 N Boston Court, while the 64-unit building permit is filed under 5601 N Chester Way.
